reason: The passage explicitly demonstrates the Hebrew people's ingratitude and disobedience toward Yahweh. Despite being provided daily manna and receiving explicit instructions about the Sabbath—including God's promise of double portions on the sixth day—the people go out to gather on the seventh day when explicitly commanded not to. This violation of God's command and failure to trust His provision manifests as ingratitude. God Himself expresses frustration, asking 'How long do you refuse to keep My commandments and My teachings?' (עַד־ אָנָה מֵֽאַנְתֶּם לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי), characterizing their disobedience as a refusal to honor His word and provision—core markers of ingratitude.
